title: CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks
content_md: ​The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies that attackers are now exploiting a recently patched critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability in the wild. Cisco Expressway Series devices are enterprise collaboration gateways (deployed as virtual machines or physical hardware appliances) that connect internal voice and video systems with outside networks and remote users via a secure connection. Tracked as CVE-2026-76466 , this security flaw stems from the use of hard-coded credentials and a failure to fully validate client certificates, enabling unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute arbitrary operating system commands as root on affected Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E devices configured in a cluster. "An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands," Cisco said in late October, when it released security patches to address the issue. While Cisco says that its Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) is not aware of active exploitation in the wild or publicly available proof-of-concept exploits targeting this vulnerability, CISA tagged it as actively exploited on Friday.
